{
  "skills": [
    {
      "skill_id": "hbond_polarity_hydration",
      "rules": [
        {
          "rule_id": "heteroatom_rich_hbond_network",
          "conditions": {"hetero_atom_bin": "hetero_high"},
          "weight": 0.85,
          "rationale": "N/O-rich solutes donate and accept several water hydrogen bonds, the dominant favorable term in hydration free energy."
        },
        {
          "rule_id": "moderate_polarity_bonus",
          "conditions": {"hetero_atom_bin": "hetero_mid"},
          "weight": 0.45,
          "rationale": "Intermediate heteroatom count supplies polar hydration sites without a large hydrophobic cavity cost."
        },
        {
          "rule_id": "polyhalogen_hydrophobic_penalty",
          "conditions": {"halogen_bin": "halogen_high"},
          "weight": -0.6,
          "rationale": "Heavily halogenated solutes are weakly hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic, giving poor hydration despite high polarizability."
        },
        {
          "rule_id": "short_nonpolar_prior_reversal",
          "conditions": {"hetero_atom_bin": "hetero_none"},
          "weight": -0.55,
          "rationale": "Reverses the weak short-SMILES source prior: heteroatom-free hydrocarbons hydrate poorly regardless of small size."
        }
      ],
      "ridge": 0.9,
      "prior_scale": 0.5,
      "semantic_mass_start": 0.45,
      "semantic_mass_end": 0.18,
      "ucb_weight": 0.55,
      "gp_beta_start": 2.0,
      "gp_beta_end": 0.9,
      "gp_xi": 0.02,
      "confidence": 0.6,
      "hypothesis": "Asserts solute-water hydrogen bonding, not molecular size, controls hydration, and downweights the low-confidence smiles_short source prior. Fails if the score rewards small nonpolar solutes or polar halogenated species."
    },
    {
      "skill_id": "esol_size_ring_transfer",
      "rules": [
        {
          "rule_id": "short_smiles_source_prior",
          "conditions": {"smiles_length_bin": "smiles_short"},
          "weight": 0.45,
          "rationale": "Source ESOL value prior gave smiles_short +6.89; small solutes pay little cavity-formation cost in water."
        },
        {
          "rule_id": "mid_smiles_source_penalty",
          "conditions": {"smiles_length_bin": "smiles_mid"},
          "weight": -0.35,
          "rationale": "Source effect for smiles_mid was -6.61; growing carbon skeleton increases hydrophobic surface area."
        },
        {
          "rule_id": "long_smiles_source_penalty",
          "conditions": {"smiles_length_bin": "smiles_long"},
          "weight": -0.55,
          "rationale": "Largest negative source effect (-11.46, confidence 0.47); long chains bury polar groups and enlarge the cavity."
        },
        {
          "rule_id": "acyclic_scaffold_bonus",
          "conditions": {"ring_token_bin": "ring_token_none"},
          "weight": 0.3,
          "rationale": "Ring role carried the highest transfer weight (0.758); acyclic flexible solutes were favored in the source task."
        }
      ],
      "ridge": 1.2,
      "prior_scale": 0.3,
      "semantic_mass_start": 0.32,
      "semantic_mass_end": 0.1,
      "ucb_weight": 0.6,
      "gp_beta_start": 2.2,
      "gp_beta_end": 1.0,
      "gp_xi": 0.01,
      "confidence": 0.35,
      "hypothesis": "Transfers ESOL size and ring roles under a shared cavity-cost mechanism. Fails if hydration ranking is polarity-driven, since short acyclic SMILES here include many alkanes and halocarbons."
    }
  ],
  "selected_skill_id": "hbond_polarity_hydration",
  "lesson": "Source roles are size and ring counts from a solubility task with weak role confidence (0.22 for length), whereas hydration free energy is mechanistically governed by solute-water hydrogen bonding, so a heteroatom/halogen polarity contrast is the safer transferred prior.",
  "revision_summary": "Rewrote both skills with schema-correct single field:value condition objects. Kept the source-faithful size/ring transfer at low semantic mass and confidence, and kept the polarity counter-hypothesis as deployment, simplifying its fourth rule from a two-field interaction to a direct hetero_none reversal so the reversal of the low-confidence short-SMILES prior is unambiguous, and trimming its starting semantic mass so the target-only GP anchor keeps most rank mass early."
}

rules.rationale: N/O-rich solutes donate and accept several water hydrogen bonds, the dominant favorable term in hydration free energy.
Intermediate heteroatom count supplies polar hydration sites without a large hydrophobic cavity cost.
Heavily halogenated solutes are weakly hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic, giving poor hydration despite high polarizability.
Reverses the weak short-SMILES source prior: heteroatom-free hydrocarbons hydrate poorly regardless of small size.

skills.hypothesis: Asserts solute-water hydrogen bonding, not molecular size, controls hydration, and downweights the low-confidence smiles_short source prior. Fails if the score rewards small nonpolar solutes or polar halogenated species.

rules.rationale: Source ESOL value prior gave smiles_short +6.89; small solutes pay little cavity-formation cost in water.
Source effect for smiles_mid was -6.61; growing carbon skeleton increases hydrophobic surface area.
Largest negative source effect (-11.46, confidence 0.47); long chains bury polar groups and enlarge the cavity.
Ring role carried the highest transfer weight (0.758); acyclic flexible solutes were favored in the source task.

skills.hypothesis: Transfers ESOL size and ring roles under a shared cavity-cost mechanism. Fails if hydration ranking is polarity-driven, since short acyclic SMILES here include many alkanes and halocarbons.

normalized.lesson: Source roles are size and ring counts from a solubility task with weak role confidence (0.22 for length), whereas hydration free energy is mechanistically governed by solute-water hydrogen bonding, so a heteroatom/halogen polarity contrast is the safer transferred prior.
normalized.revision_summary: Rewrote both skills with schema-correct single field:value condition objects. Kept the source-faithful size/ring transfer at low semantic mass and confidence, and kept the polarity counter-hypothesis as deployment, simplifying its fourth rule from a two-field interaction to a direct hetero_none reversal so the reversal of the low-confidence short-SMILES prior is unambiguous, and trimming its starting semantic mass so the target-only GP anchor keeps most rank mass early.
